rawAnswer: {"findings":[{"kind":"defect","severity":"high","title":"Inverted accessibility check flags every public keyed property as non-public","detail":"In GetObjectInfo, the keyed-property branch changed from != Accessibility.Public to == Accessibility.Public. The requirement does not ask for this. nonPublicMembersAreSerialized is now set whenever a type has a public [Key] property, which is almost every [MessagePackObject] type. The comment above the line and the matching field branch at line 1120 still use !=. Effects: (1) Line 1352 now reports MessagePackObjectAllowPrivateRequired on ordinary public types. (2) Non-public unkeyed members start producing MemberNeedsKey, and deferred diagnostics get flushed. (3) At line 1382, nestedFormatterRequired && nonPublicMembersAreSerialized now runs the partial-type check for public properties with private setters. For example, KeysMustBeUnique or DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys are raised for members inherited from a metadata base type. Those fall back to a null location from DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault(), and the consuming project's real key collision would no longer be reported. Analyzers are allowed to report Location.None. Only locations in syntax trees outside the compilation are forbidden. The filter should drop only in-source locations whose tree is not in the compilation, not every diagnostic without a location.
